perf.summary: JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount is read twice in the ctor (size calc and loop bound) and once per loop check; hoist to a local. Same pattern in Dispose.
perf.currentCost: JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount appears in the totalSize expression and as the loop condition (re-evaluated each iteration if the JIT cannot prove the property is pure). Property accesses are not always inlined/CSE'd under Burst.
perf.proposedChange: int count = JobsUtility.ThreadIndexCount; use 'count' for totalSize, the init loop bound, and in Dispose. Same for ThreadRandom.
perf.rationale: Guarantees a single read of the property and a loop with a register-resident bound, enabling the compiler to better optimize the init loop; avoids repeated property dispatch the JIT may not hoist.
perf.risk: ThreadIndexCount is a fixed process-wide count, so caching it within a single ctor/Dispose call is safe. No semantic change.
